chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: A man enters the mosque when the people have already prayed; should he give the adhan and iqamah? He said: “If he entered and the row has not yet dispersed, he should pray with their adhan and their iqamah. But if the row has dispersed, he should give the adhan and the iqamah.”

key_terms.أَيُؤَذِّنُ: whether he should pronounce the adhan
key_terms.إِقَامَتِهِمْ: with reliance on their iqamah already given
key_terms.الصَّفُّ: the prayer row of the congregation
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, the place where the prayer is being joined or followed
key_terms.بِأَذَانِهِمْ: with reliance on their adhan already given
key_terms.يُقِيمُ: whether he should pronounce the iqamah for prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone enters the mosque after the congregation has finished, should he recite the adhan and iqamah again?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who enters the mosque after the congregational prayer has already been performed. If the prayer rows are still intact, he may rely on the existing adhan and iqamah; if the rows have dispersed, he should recite his own adhan and iqamah.
